methods.label: Put larger digits in higher places
methods.explanation:
Each digit contributes its place value to the sum. If a larger digit occupies a lower place than a smaller digit, exchanging them increases the sum: the difference between the digits becomes worth more in the higher place.

Therefore the two largest digits must occupy the two ten-thousands places. The next two largest must occupy the thousands places, and so on. The required pairs, from highest place to lowest, are
\[
\{8,9\},\quad \{6,7\},\quad \{4,5\},\quad \{2,3\},\quad \{0,1\}.
\]
Any allocation violating this order can be improved by a swap, while every allocation using these pairs has the same sum.

Among the choices, only \(87431\) takes one digit from each pair in the required order. Its companion can be \(96520\), and together they use every digit exactly once:
\[
87431+96520=183951.
\]
Thus \(87431\) can be one of the numbers, choice \(\text{C}\).
